data.text:
This is a list of commands and instructions from a cursor from other project I have (see bellow). Investigate if ddflow could work and coordinate with such external instructions in cursor or any other agent or IDE, and verify if you could take any inspirations to extend this project, for example this project commands or mcp commands exposed to the user:

[followed by pasted .cursor/rules/*.mdc (api-openapi, ask-ai-surface, branch-lifecycle, bugtracking, buildsuccess, changelog, configurable-constants, database-migrations, default-branch-main, docker-testing, docker, external-access-throttle, git, gitea, outbound-throttle-common, probe-research-hypotheses, rubber-ducking, security, table-visualization, todo, ui-graph, ui-testing, ui, workflow-orchestration) and .cursor/commands/*.md (bug-hunting, check-with-guides, code-clean, commit-all, deduplicate-code, docker-compose-inspect, run-tests, ui-test-sync-execute, upgrade-to-latest-versions) from the ai-bond project]

data.summary: One [[macro]] whose name collides with a shipped command (e.g. code-clean) makes load_macros raise; macro_commands() swallows it and returns {}, so EVERY macro vanishes from prompts list and MCP prompts/list, `ddflow prompts show <valid-macro>` says "unknown prompt" (resolve_any checks the swallowed all_commands first, so the promised error never surfaces), and doctor exits 0 without mentioning it. The refusal written to stop silent shadowing is itself silent. Repro: two macros, one named code-clean, one bug-hunting -> prompts show bug-hunting = unknown prompt. Also: prompts list prints the path of a prompt_file macro as "None".

Importer _LESSON_HEAD matches L\d+ only, so hyphenated ids (## L-359 — ..., ## R-52 — ...) are not read as ids: they import as L-l-359-agent-branches-... / R-r-52-..., so "see L-359" cross-references do not resolve, and a lessons-summary bullet citing exactly one lesson "(L-359)" is not attached as its summary but imported as a duplicate lesson tagged summary. Probed on a fixture shaped like the ai-bond project.

data.text: Investigation: ddflow alongside a Cursor-rules project (ai-bond). Probed on a fixture: (1) [[macro]] prompt_file=".cursor/commands/x.md" serves a Cursor command to every MCP client with no code change -- works; (2) importer ignores TODOS.md (knob todo_globs fixes it; **STATUS**: PLAN sessions import as open phases), ignores .cursor/rules and .cursor/commands, and mangles hyphenated L-NNN/R-NNN ids (B-import-hyphen-ids); (3) macro name clash drops all macros silently (B-macro-clash-silent). Proposed, not filed: rules inventory across agents (who sees which rule, always-loaded cost), .mdc globs -> decisions, commands bridge both ways (adopt writes .cursor/commands; command_dirs auto-discovery), path-scoped gates (when_globs), co-change obligations (CHANGELOG/UITESTS.md/OpenAPI), one-way issue-tracker sink (Gitea/GitHub/Linear, relates B173), structured evidence fields for agent gates. Conflicts to resolve by editing the project rules, not ddflow: TODOS.md/Gitea/LOG.md as second source of truth, cursor/* branch lifecycle vs claim+merge, no precedence between alwaysApply rules.
add the ideas work taking as tasks we could work on in the task list

data.body: Operator 2026-09-29, after investigating ddflow beside the ai-bond project's 24 alwaysApply Cursor rules and 9 .cursor/commands. Findings probed on a fixture of that layout (session s20260929T110813-3436541): a [[macro]] with prompt_file pointing at .cursor/commands already serves a Cursor command to every MCP client; the importer skips TODOS.md, .cursor/rules and .cursor/commands and mangles hyphenated L-NNN/R-NNN ids; a colliding macro silently drops every macro. Conflicts that stay the project's to resolve (not ddflow's): a second source of truth (TODOS.md/Gitea/LOG.md), cursor/* branch lifecycle vs claim+merge, and no precedence among alwaysApply rules — the rules inventory should REPORT these, not rewrite anyone's rules.
data.title: Coexist with a project's own agent rules and commands (Cursor .mdc/.cursor/commands and other agents' native surfaces)

data.body: Repro: two macros, one named code-clean (shipped), one bug-hunting -> prompts list shows neither, prompts show bug-hunting says 'unknown prompt', doctor exits 0. Wanted: the valid macros still load; the clashing one is refused BY NAME on prompts list/show, over MCP prompts/list (as a visible note, not a dropped list) and in doctor as a PROBLEM. Also: prompts list prints a prompt_file macro's path as 'None' — show the file. Regression tests must fail on current main.
data.title: A [[macro]] named like a shipped command is reported, not silently dropping every macro (fixes bug B-macro-clash-silent)

data.body: _LESSON_HEAD matches L\d+ only: '## L-359 — …' imports as L-l-359-agent-branches-…, '## R-52 — …' as R-r-52-…, and a lessons-summary bullet citing '(L-359)' becomes a duplicate lesson tagged summary instead of that lesson's summary. Accept L-NNN / R-NNN (and keep L123), and the summary-citation matcher must use the same id grammar. Idempotency: ids that already imported under the slug form must not re-import as duplicates — check what import --verify says on a log imported before the fix.
data.title: Importer keeps hyphenated ids (L-359, R-52) as ids, so cross-references and one-lesson summary bullets resolve (fixes bug B-import-hyphen-ids)

data.body: Projects driven by Cursor rules keep TODOS.md (plural) with '## Session N (date): …' + '**STATUS**: PLAN|IN PROGRESS|SHIPPED' and a root LOG.md journal; neither is in TODO_GLOBS/JOURNAL_GLOBS, so the queue starts empty for them. Probed: with todo_globs=["TODOS.md"] a PLAN session imports as an open phase with its boxes as tasks. Add the defaults; confirm SHIPPED-over-unticked is reported like other phase headings; check LOG.md is not a generated index in the projects measured before (upper-case LOG.md at root vs docs/LOG.md).
data.title: Importer reads TODOS.md and root LOG.md by default; **STATUS**: session headers carry their disposition

data.body: The project's OWN rules bind only the agent whose surface they live in: 24 .cursor/rules/*.mdc reach Cursor and never Claude Code, Codex or Gemini in the same repo. Read-only report over .cursor/rules/*.mdc (frontmatter: alwaysApply/globs/description), .cursor/commands, .claude/commands, .clinerules/, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .windsurf/rules, .tabnine/guidelines, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/QWEN.md/GEMINI.md: per file, which adopted agents load it and when (always / by glob / on request); per agent, the always-loaded size (bytes and an approximate token count, labelled approximate); and rules that restate a ddflow-owned workflow (todo lists, issue logging, branch lifecycle, lessons files) as NOTES naming the file — conflicts are the operator's to resolve, ddflow never edits them. CLI + MCP from one implementation; a doctor note only when an adopted agent sees none of the project's rules that another adopted agent sees. Reuse adopt.NATIVE_RULES rather than a second table.
data.title: ddflow rules: inventory every agent's native rule and command files — who loads what, always-loaded cost, and rules that restate ddflow-owned workflow

data.body: An .mdc with globs: frontmatter is exactly a decision --globs: brief and decision applicable already surface it to the item touching those files. Import them (new source family, rule_globs knob, default .cursor/rules/*.mdc) as decisions that REFERENCE the file (source=path:line, body = description + first section, not a copy of a 700-line rule), idempotent like every other family. alwaysApply rules are NOT decisions: report them via the rules inventory instead. Never delete or rewrite the .mdc. Reuse the frontmatter parser from B-rules-inventory.
data.title: Import glob-scoped .cursor/rules/*.mdc as decisions with globs, so brief surfaces them to EVERY agent on the tasks they govern

data.body: AGENT_COMMANDS only has claude -> .claude/commands/implement.md. Cursor reads .cursor/commands/*.md as slash commands (the ai-bond project uses nine). Write implement (and whichever other shipped commands make sense) with the DDFLOW:MANAGED mark; keep an operator's own file of the same name (ai-bond has /code-clean and /bug-hunting of its own) exactly as _write_command already does for Claude. Research first whether Cursor also surfaces MCP prompts as slash commands — if it does, say so in the delta doc and consider whether the file is still needed.
data.title: adopt writes ddflow's workflow commands into .cursor/commands/ for Cursor, as it does .claude/commands/ for Claude Code

data.body: Probed: [[macro]] prompt_file=".cursor/commands/bug-hunting.md" already works, one block per command. command_dirs discovers *.md in the listed dirs as macros (name = file stem, title/description from frontmatter or first line, source shown in prompts list). A name that collides with a shipped command (ai-bond's code-clean) is reported by name and skipped — never shadows, never silently drops the rest (that is B-fix-macro-clash-silent). ddflow's own DDFLOW:MANAGED files are skipped, or the shipped command would appear twice.
data.title: [prompts] command_dirs: serve a project's existing slash-command files (.cursor/commands, .claude/commands) as MCP prompts to every agent, with no TOML per command

data.body: 'If you touch the API, validate OpenAPI and run route tests'; 'if you touch ui/, rebuild that image'; 'if you touch the schema, a migration must exist' — today such a gate is always on or skipped by hand on every item, which trains skipping. Decide on the change's ACTUAL paths (the diff against base, plus untracked), not only the declared globs, since globs can under-declare. A gate that does not apply is recorded with its own outcome and the evidence (which paths, which patterns) — never silently absent, per 'silence is not a pass'. Re-evaluate at complete: a later commit that brings the item into scope must bring the gate back. gate verify / mutations unchanged.
data.title: Path-scoped gates: [gate.X] when_globs puts a gate in an item's pipeline only when the item's change touches those paths

data.body: A mechanical, checkable rule behind many hand-written ones: user-visible change -> CHANGELOG.md; ui/tests/e2e/** <-> UITESTS.md; src/routes/** -> api/openapi.yaml; docs/lessons.md -> its table of contents. Shape to research: a built-in gate kind [gate.X] cochange = { when = [...], also = [...] } built on B-gate-when-globs' path evaluation, reporting which side moved alone. Relates to B174 (CHANGELOG / version files) — check whether that should consume this.
data.title: Co-change checks: when paths X change, paths Y must change in the same item (CHANGELOG, UITESTS.md with e2e specs, openapi.yaml with routes, lessons TOC)

data.body: Projects that make an issue tracker 'the ultimate log' spend hundreds of lines of rules making the agent hand-post each step; ddflow already records every step. A [tracker] sink posts them: link an item to an issue (--issue or a trailer), comment on claim / each gate outcome / merge (with SHA) / complete, and CLOSE only if [tracker] close_on_complete is set (default off). The event log stays the source of truth; the tracker is never read back as state. An outage is recorded and retried later, never fails a gate or blocks complete, and never loses a comment. Relates to B173 (Gitea/Forgejo forge adapter): share the CLI/token plumbing, keep PR merging and issue mirroring separate. Research gate: Gitea API vs tea CLI, GitHub via gh, Linear via its API.
data.title: One-way issue-tracker sink: mirror claim, gate outcomes and completion onto a linked Gitea / GitHub / Linear issue as comments

data.body: Agent gates rest on their evidence contract; today that is prose, so 'LGTM' passes. [gate.X] evidence_fields = [...] makes gate record refuse a pass missing a field (empty or boilerplate-only values count as missing), lists every missing field at once, and stores the fields structured so recall and the review can read them. Ship a sensible default for rubber_duck and critic only if it does not break existing projects' recorded passes (applies to new records only).
data.title: Required evidence fields for agent gates: e.g. rubber_duck must record intent, change map, assumptions challenged, edge cases, verification, fresh-eyes findings

data.body: One section, written last so it describes what shipped: how ddflow reads a project's .mdc rules and command files, what it replaces (enforced equivalents: cross-family review, regression-test-per-bug, probe-before-plan, unavailable-not-passed, cadences), what stays the operator's to resolve (second source of truth, branch lifecycle, alwaysApply precedence), with a worked example based on the ai-bond layout. Update the How do I… table and the command reference.
data.title: Document coexisting with a project's own agent rules: README section + Cursor delta, incl. which of a project's rules ddflow replaces and which conflicts stay the operator's

data.text: Make sure all the ideas and tasks are generalized so they could be applied to any project and not having the explicit specifics of the cursor project they were taken from

data.body: A project that adopts ddflow usually already has instructions of its own: always-loaded or path-scoped rule files, slash-command files, a todo file, a lessons file, an issue tracker it treats as the log. Today ddflow neither reads nor accounts for them, so (a) a rule written for one agent never reaches the others working in the same repository, (b) the project's commands exist in one IDE only, (c) path-triggered policies ('touch X, then check Y') can only be encoded as gates that are always on or skipped by hand, and (d) the project's own history imports lossily. This phase makes ddflow read, report and bridge those surfaces for any project and any agent. Out of scope, deliberately: rewriting a project's rules. Where they conflict with ddflow's workflow (a second source of truth for the queue, a different branch lifecycle, several always-loaded rules with no precedence between them) ddflow REPORTS the conflict and the operator resolves it.
data.title: Coexist with a project's own agent rules and slash commands, whichever agents and IDEs it already uses

data.body: Default TODO_GLOBS/JOURNAL_GLOBS miss common variants — plural TODOS.md, a root-level LOG.md — so for such a project the queue starts empty until the operator finds the knob. Probed: with todo_globs set, a '## Session N (date): …' heading with '**STATUS**: PLAN' imports as an open phase with its boxes as tasks. Survey the spellings projects actually use before adding defaults (a default that matches a generated file is worse than none), confirm a SHIPPED status over unticked boxes is reported like other phase headings, and that a LOG.md which is a generated index is still dropped.
data.title: Importer covers more common todo/journal spellings by default (TODOS.md, root LOG.md) and reads '**STATUS**:' lines under session-style headings

data.body: A rule file scoped to paths (e.g. a frontmatter globs: list) is exactly a decision --globs: brief and decision applicable already surface it to the item touching those files, whichever agent holds it. Import them as a new source family (rule_globs knob; defaults = the path-scoped rule formats the agents ddflow supports actually have) as decisions that REFERENCE the file (source=path:line, body = description + first section, not a copy of a long rule), idempotent like every other family. Always-loaded rules are NOT decisions: report them via the rules inventory. Never delete or rewrite the source file. Reuse the frontmatter parser from B-rules-inventory.

data.body: A common policy shape is 'if you touch these paths, run this check' — an API change needs its contract validated, a schema change needs a migration, a change under a container's source needs that image rebuilt. Today such a gate is always on or skipped by hand on every item, which trains skipping. Decide on the change's ACTUAL paths (the diff against base, plus untracked), not only the declared globs, since globs can under-declare. A gate that does not apply is recorded with its own outcome and the evidence (which paths, which patterns) — never silently absent, per 'silence is not a pass'. Re-evaluate at complete: a later commit that brings the item into scope must bring the gate back. gate verify / mutations unchanged.

A mechanical, checkable rule behind many hand-written ones: a user-visible change must add a changelog entry; an API route change must update the API spec; a test-requirements document and the tests generated from it move together; a lessons or docs file and its index move together. Shape to research: a built-in gate kind [gate.X] cochange = { when = [...], also = [...] } built on B-gate-when-globs' path evaluation, reporting which side moved alone. Relates to B174 (CHANGELOG / version files) — check whether that should consume this.
data.title: Co-change checks: when paths X change, paths Y must change in the same item (changelog, API spec, test specs, docs index)

data.body: Some projects treat an issue tracker as the log of record and spend a lot of instruction text making the agent hand-post each step; ddflow already records every step. A [tracker] sink posts them: link an item to an issue (--issue or a trailer), comment on claim / each gate outcome / merge (with SHA) / complete, and CLOSE only if [tracker] close_on_complete is set (default off). The event log stays the source of truth; the tracker is never read back as state. An outage is recorded and retried later, never fails a gate or blocks complete, and never loses a comment. Pluggable per tracker (start with whichever forges ddflow already talks to; Gitea/Forgejo, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira are candidates). Relates to B173 (more forge adapters): share the CLI/token plumbing, keep PR merging and issue mirroring separate.

Agent gates rest on their evidence contract; today that is prose, so 'LGTM' passes. [gate.X] evidence_fields = [...] makes gate record refuse a pass missing a field (empty or boilerplate-only values count as missing), lists every missing field at once, and stores the fields structured so recall and later reviews can read them. The field names are the project's to choose; ship a default for review gates only if it does not break existing projects' recorded passes (applies to new records only).
data.title: Required evidence fields for agent gates: a review must record named parts (intent, what changed, assumptions challenged, edge cases, verification, findings), not a bare pass
